Q: Do we need to create a custom class for OAUTH in kafka connect cluster to authenticate Confluent kafka connect from a custom managed kafka A:

No. Confluent Platform 8.1+ includes built-in Azure Managed Identity support for Java clients via io.confluent.security.auth.client.oauth.UamiJwtRetriever, so no custom class is required.

So for a Kafka Connect worker, use the worker’s Kafka client configs (producer.*, consumer.*, and if needed admin.*) with SASL/OAUTHBEARER, and point sasl.oauthbearer.token.endpoint.url to Azure IMDS. Also set the JVM system property org.apache.kafka.sasl.oauthbearer.allowed.urls to the same IMDS URL.

The standard org.apache.kafka.common.security.oauthbearer.OAuthBearerLoginCallbackHandler shown in the generic Connect OAuth docs is for the usual client-id/client-secret OAuth flow, not specifically for Azure Managed Identity.

This applies to Confluent Platform only. Confluent Cloud and Apache Kafka OSS handle managed identity differently.

Confluent references:

  • https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/security/authentication/sasl/oauthbearer/uami.html

  • https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/security/authentication/oauth-oidc/configure-connect.html

Q: How to Minimize .NET MAUI App to Dock When Clicking Red Close Button on Mac Catalyst A:

Mac Catalyst doesn't natively support minimizing to dock when clicking the red close button .It closes/quits the app instead. However, you can work around this by intercepting the event.

Add this in the project file and then clean solution and rebuild it and then try it.

<key>UISupportsDocumentBrowser</key>

<true/>

Q: Is it possible to add and show new status "PARTIAL PASS" in Playwright HTML report? A:

Playwright closed that feature request so native support isn't coming. Custom reporter via the Reporter API is the way, you handle onTestEnd, tag tests with annotations, and map your own status logic from there. Rolling your own gives you full control over the HTML structure and how that status gets displayed.

Q: How to make an image act like a button in html, so that when pressed it causes an animation to run? A:

The easiest way to achieve something like this for a beginner, would probably be to use a details element - instead of text, you can put an image into the summary element.

And getting the contents of a details element to open with some sort of animation - that should not be a completely new topic; I'm sure you'll find something regarding that with a little bit of research.
